answer.generated: Two key design issues in distributed systems engineering are transparency and openness. Transparency concerns the extent to which the distributed system appears as a single system to the user, determining when it is beneficial for users to be aware of the system's distributed nature. Openness involves whether the system should adhere to standard protocols supporting interoperability or utilize more specialized protocols that offer greater design flexibility but potentially reduce compatibility with other systems.
